whatsthis.title: What's this?
whatsthis.text: Tap the ? in any window's title bar, then tap anything: a button, a slider, an icon, a song, a taskbar item, a Start menu entry. You get a short explanation instead of the thing happening. Tap ? and then a title bar to hear about the whole window. The Start menu has its own What's this? entry, so you can ask about menu items too.

win-close.title: Close (skull)
win-close.text: Closes this window. Nothing is lost: songs keep playing and the box keeps running. Open it again from the desktop icons or the Start menu.

win-player.title: PLAYER.EXE
win-player.text: The music player. It opens first. It lists the songs on the box's SD card and plays them either on this phone or, if the box has Bluetooth, out of the box's own speaker.

win-speaker.title: SPEAKER.EXE
win-speaker.text: The box's Bluetooth speaker: find a speaker, choose it, and see whether it is connected. Also has the Optimize switch. Only boxes built with Bluetooth have a speaker to set up.

win-network.title: NETWORK.EXE
win-network.text: Which Wi-Fi the box is on, the networks it remembers, and adding a new one. Changing anything needs this phone to be paired with the box first.

win-matrix.title: MATRIX.EXE
win-matrix.text: A picture of the 8 by 8 light panel, drawn exactly as the box computes it. It works with no panel attached, and it only asks the box for frames while this window is open. The real LED driver is switched off in the current firmware, so this window is the only place the lights show.

win-games.title: GAMES
win-games.text: A folder of games. They live on the SD card under /game and open in their own browser tab. A game greys out until the box confirms the files are on the card.

win-driveb.title: DRIVE B:
win-driveb.text: A drive recovered from the crashed ENIAS. Its files are scrambled until the ship's neural net is aligned enough to read them. The net realigns as you listen to the band's songs on the box. The big number is how far along it is.

win-help.title: HELP
win-help.text: An index of every feature, including ones with no button on screen: the BOOT button, the speaker's own buttons, saved networks, the alignment rules. Tap a line to open it.

icon-driveb.title: DRIVE B icon
icon-driveb.text: Opens the recovered drive from the ENIAS.

start-button.title: START
start-button.text: Opens the Start menu: every window, the screen look setting, Help and What's this?. Tap it again or tap anywhere else to close the menu.

start-driveb.title: Drive B
start-driveb.text: Opens the recovered drive. Its files unlock as the ENIAS aligns.

start-network.title: Network
start-network.text: Opens the Wi-Fi window. It is highlighted orange with the note needs setup when the box has no network saved.

start-matrix.title: Matrix lights
start-matrix.text: Opens the 8 by 8 light panel window.

start-lens.title: Screen: tube or clean
start-lens.text: Switches the whole page between the tube look (scanlines, a little color fringing, noise, a dark rim, a slow rolling band) and a clean look with none of it. Use clean if the tube look is hard to read or the page feels slow. The choice is remembered on this phone only.

start-whatsthis.title: What's this?
start-whatsthis.text: Turns on What's this? mode from inside the Start menu: your next tap explains the thing you tap instead of doing it. Handy for asking about the menu entries themselves.

taskbar-task.title: Taskbar item
taskbar-task.text: One per open window. Tap it to bring that window to the front and scroll to it. Closing a window removes its item.

tray.title: Clock
tray.text: The time on this phone. It reads NO WI-FI in orange when the box has no network saved.

play-toggle.title: Play and Pause
play-toggle.text: Pauses the song, or plays it again. It reads Pause while a song is playing and Play while it is paused.

play-next.title: Next
play-next.text: Skips to the next song in the list. On the last song there is no next.

play-seek.title: Position slider
play-seek.text: Shows how far into the song you are. Drag it to jump to another point in the song.

play-volume.title: Volume slider
play-volume.text: Volume for the song playing, on this phone or on the box's speaker, whichever is playing it. The setting is remembered on this phone.

play-on.title: Play songs on
play-on.text: Where songs come out. This device plays them in this phone's browser. The box's speaker plays them from the SD card out of the box's Bluetooth speaker, and this page becomes a remote. The choice only appears on a box built with Bluetooth, and it is remembered on this phone.

matrix-preview.title: Matrix preview
matrix-preview.text: A tiny picture of the light panel. It makes no requests of its own. Tap it to open the Matrix window.

sd-track.title: A song on the box
sd-track.text: Tap a song to play it. The one playing is highlighted orange. Songs play in list order and the next one starts by itself.

sd-delete.title: Delete
sd-delete.text: Deletes this song from the box's SD card, after asking you to confirm. It cannot be undone.

sd-pick.title: Upload songs
sd-pick.text: Choose audio files on this phone to copy onto the box's SD card. 24-bit and 32-bit WAVs are converted to 16-bit in your browser first, at their own sample rate, so they fit the Bluetooth path. Other files are sent as they are.

sd-key.title: Pairing key
sd-key.text: Uploading or deleting can be locked to phones that hold the box's pairing key. Joining the box's own hotspot fills it in for you. Or paste it here. It is saved on this phone only.

sd-key-save.title: Save key
sd-key-save.text: Saves the pairing key you typed on this phone, so uploads and deletes are accepted.

net-refresh.title: Refresh
net-refresh.text: Asks the box again which network it is on and re-draws this window.

net-open-page.title: Open in browser
net-open-page.text: Opens the box's page in your phone's normal browser at the box's current address. From a phone's pop-up sign-in sheet this is the way out to the full browser.

net-host-mode.title: Host its own network
net-host-mode.text: Takes the box off the Wi-Fi it is on and has it serve its own network, Lakehorse Radio, with the page at http://192.168.4.1/. Nothing is forgotten: the saved networks stay in the list. Join Lakehorse Radio on this phone, then tap Use now on a saved network to put the box back on Wi-Fi. Restarting the box also puts it back on a saved network.

net-forget.title: Forget this network
net-forget.text: Makes the box forget the network it is on now. It asks first. If it was the only network saved, the box starts its own Lakehorse Radio hotspot, so this page may stop answering. Only a paired phone may do this.

net-row.title: Network in range
net-row.text: A Wi-Fi network the box can hear, strongest first. Tap one to choose it, then type its password and tap Join. The bars show signal strength.

net-saved-use.title: Use now
net-saved-use.text: Tells the box to leave its current network and join this saved one right away. This page stops answering on the old network, so switch the phone to the same network too. Only a paired phone may do this.

net-saved-forget.title: Forget (saved network)
net-saved-forget.text: Removes this network from the box's list of saved networks. Only a paired phone may do this.

net-manual.title: Type the name
net-manual.text: Use this for a network that did not appear in the list, such as a phone hotspot that is switched off right now or a hidden network. Type its exact name.

net-pass.title: Password
net-pass.text: The network's Wi-Fi password, 8 to 63 characters. Leave it empty for an open network. Passwords are case sensitive.

net-show-pass.title: Show password
net-show-pass.text: Shows the password you typed so you can check it.

net-host.title: Name on the network
net-host.text: The box's name on your network. You reach it at this name followed by .local, for example lakehorseradio.local. Letters, numbers and hyphens only.

net-join.title: Join
net-join.text: Saves this network and joins it. The box remembers up to 5 networks and joins whichever it can hear. If you are on the box's own hotspot, the hotspot goes away a few seconds after it joins.

net-rescan.title: Scan networks
net-rescan.text: A phone cannot be seen sharing its own hotspot while it is showing this page, so to use this phone's hotspot, type its name and password instead. Looks for Wi-Fi networks in range. Scanning retunes the radio, which can interrupt music playing from the box for a few seconds.

net-cancel.title: Cancel
net-cancel.text: Clears the network you picked and what you typed.

net-help.title: Box cannot find or join a network?
net-help.text: Opens tips for the usual causes: the box only works with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, how to switch a phone hotspot to 2.4 GHz, WPA3-only routers, and hotel Wi-Fi with a sign-in page, which the box cannot use.

net-pair.title: Pair this phone
net-pair.text: Pairs this phone with the box so it may change networks. The box only allows it for 2 minutes after you hold its BOOT button for 3 seconds or unplug it and plug it back in, which proves you are at the box. While the box is being built, changing networks is open to everyone and this button is hidden; a setting in config.h turns the lock back on.

spk-link.title: Speaker connection button
spk-link.text: Connects to the chosen speaker or, when Bluetooth is off, turns it back on. It only appears when it has something to do.

spk-find.title: Find speakers
spk-find.text: Scans for Bluetooth speakers for about 14 seconds. Put your speaker in pairing mode first. The ones found appear below.

spk-device.title: A speaker found
spk-device.text: Tap to choose this speaker. The box remembers it and connects to it by itself next time it starts.

spk-optimize.title: Optimize for this device
spk-optimize.text: Ticked means Bluetooth is off, which makes the page and downloads much faster on this phone but silences the box's speaker. Changing it restarts the box, about 10 seconds, and the page waits and reconnects by itself. It asks first.

matrix-mode-bars.title: Bars
matrix-mode-bars.text: Eight columns that follow the music: from the box when it plays the song itself, from this page when your phone plays it. With nothing playing it shows a demo pattern.

matrix-mode-title.title: Title
matrix-mode-title.text: Scrolls the name of the song playing, or LAKEHORSE when nothing is.

matrix-mode-dazzle.title: Dazzle
matrix-mode-dazzle.text: A drifting camouflage pattern that swells with the music.

matrix-mode-clock.title: Clock
matrix-mode-clock.text: Shows this phone's time: hours for three seconds, then minutes for three. A lit pixel in the top right corner marks hours and the bottom row counts seconds.

matrix-mode-test.title: Test
matrix-mode-test.text: Four lit corners (red, green, blue, white) on a dim grid, for checking a real panel's wiring.

matrix-mode-alignment.title: Align
matrix-mode-alignment.text: The ENIAS alignment pattern, drawn from the box's saved total. At low alignment the points are dim and scattered, wandering. As the total rises they settle one at a time into a bright steady block growing from the bottom left corner. It matches the node lattice in Drive B.

matrix-bright.title: Brightness
matrix-bright.text: How strongly the lights are drawn in this window and, when a real panel is connected, how bright it is. Lit lights never go fully dark. The real panel caps its brightness for power safety.

matrix-full.title: Full view
matrix-full.text: Fills the screen with the lights. Tap them to leave.

matrix-close.title: Close (Matrix)
matrix-close.text: Closes the window and stops asking the box for frames.

game-swim.title: Lakehorse Swimulator
game-swim.text: Opens the swimming game in a new tab. It loads from the SD card in about 10 seconds. Songs on the card are its soundtrack. Greyed out means the game files are not on the card.

game-guber.title: Guber Eats
game-guber.text: Opens the delivery driving game in a new tab, with touch or gamepad controls. Songs on the card are its soundtrack. Greyed out means the game files are not on the card.

driveb-file.title: A file on Drive B
driveb-file.text: Tap a file to open it. While it is still scrambled it shows a damaged name and a status, and tapping only stutters with a read error. Once the ENIAS is aligned enough it reads cleanly and opens: text in a small viewer, downloads as a normal download, links in a new tab.

driveb-viewer-close.title: Close file viewer
driveb-viewer-close.text: Closes the open text file and goes back to the file list.

driveb-net.title: Neural net lattice
driveb-net.text: 64 nodes, one per unit of alignment. Teal filled nodes are locked and joined to locked neighbours by thin lines. Orange rings are still drifting. The same nodes light in the same order on the matrix Align pattern.

driveb-percent.title: Alignment percent
driveb-percent.text: How far the ENIAS has realigned, read from the box. It is saved on the box, so every phone sees the same number.

driveb-log.title: Event log
driveb-log.text: The last few things the ENIAS noticed, worked out from what this page sees: signals accepted, or a pattern it did not recognise.

help-entry.title: A Help line
help-entry.text: Tap a line to open it and read more. Tap it again to fold it up.

boot-button-pairing.title: BOOT button pairing
boot-button-pairing.text: On the box's dev board, hold the BOOT button for 3 seconds. For the next 2 minutes the box will hand its pairing key to any phone on the same network that asks, through Pair this phone in the Network window. This is how the box checks you are really standing at it.

power-on-pairing.title: Pairing when the box is powered on
power-on-pairing.text: Unplug the box and plug it in again. That opens the same 2 minute pairing window as the BOOT button. A restart caused from this page does not count, because a page can cause it. Within the window, open the Network window on your phone and tap Pair this phone.

speaker-buttons.title: The speaker's own buttons
speaker-buttons.text: When the box plays songs out of its Bluetooth speaker, the speaker's own buttons work as remote controls: Play toggles play and pause, Pause and Stop pause, Forward skips to the next song and Back restarts the song. Some speakers send Play for both directions of the Play and Pause button, which is why Play toggles.

saved-networks.title: Saved networks
saved-networks.text: The box remembers up to 5 Wi-Fi networks and joins the strongest one it can hear when it starts, then walks the list in turn if it loses it. Joining a network moves it to the front. Add networks in the Network window, including your phone's hotspot. Saved passwords never leave the box. Only names are shown.

phone-hotspot.title: Joining a phone hotspot
phone-hotspot.text: Add your phone's hotspot as a saved network while you are at home, then away from home turn the hotspot on and the box finds it by itself. On an iPhone, switch on Maximize Compatibility (the box only uses 2.4 GHz) and keep the Personal Hotspot screen open while the box joins. If lakehorseradio.local does not open on the hotspot, try 172.20.10.2, then .3, .4 and so on.

hotspot-setup-boot.title: Hotspot setup boot
hotspot-setup-boot.text: If the box is on no network and a phone joins its own Lakehorse Radio hotspot while Bluetooth is running, the box restarts once with Bluetooth off for that boot only, because the hotspot cannot serve pages with Bluetooth on. The speaker is silent while you set up a network. A while after the box joins one, or once the hotspot has sat empty for a few minutes, it restarts again with Bluetooth back.

alignment-scoring.title: Alignment scoring
alignment-scoring.text: Only the band's flagged songs count. Songs the box plays on its speaker are counted by the box. Songs this phone plays from the card are counted from what was actually listened to, so skipping ahead to the end earns nothing, and a song played on this phone while the box also plays one is never counted twice. A flagged song played to the end is worth one full node (100 points). Stopped or skipped after the halfway mark it is worth 10 points. Stopped before halfway it is worth nothing. Songs not on the flag list are ignored. There are 64 nodes, 6400 points, and the percent is points over 6400 rounded down. The same song counted twice within 10 seconds counts once. Game levels will count at the same weight once the games report them: a cleared level is 100 points and an attempt of at least 10 seconds that ends without a clear is 5. The total is saved on the box.

band-tracks-json.title: band-tracks.json
band-tracks-json.text: A file on the SD card that lists the songs which count for alignment: {"version":1,"tracks":["Song.wav",...]} with exact file names, capital letters included. A missing, empty or broken file means nothing counts. A 4 KB maximum. Songs you add yourself are not on the list, so they never count. The list can be replaced from a computer with tools/push_card_file.py while on the same network.

alignment-pattern.title: Alignment pattern (matrix)
alignment-pattern.text: The Align mode on the light panel. Every node of the ENIAS net is one light. Locked nodes are bright and steady, the rest wander dimly around their own spot, and the wandering shrinks as alignment rises. The node being earned glows brighter as its share fills. Locked nodes appear from the bottom left corner outward, in the same order as the lattice in Drive B.

tube-look.title: The tube look
tube-look.text: The page is dressed as an old control screen seen through glass: scanlines, faint red and cyan fringes on text, noise, a dark rim, a slow green band rolling down and an occasional jump. It never blocks a tap and it stops moving if your phone is set to reduce motion. Switch to the clean look any time in the Start menu under Screen.

drive-b-json.title: data/drive-b.json (Drive B's files)
drive-b-json.text: The list of files on Drive B is a plain file the page reads, so the story can change without code. Each file has a name, a threshold in alignment percent, a kind (text, download or link) and its content or URL. Edit it in the project's data folder and reflash the page image.
